payRules.title: Pay rule formulas
payRules.subtitle: How each pay component is calculated — review, switch on or off, and add formulas
payRules.priorityHint: Higher wins when multiple rules apply
payRules.descriptionHint: Optional note so this rule can be recognised without reading the formula
payRules.descriptionPlaceholder: e.g. Employee social security contribution, capped at the yearly ceiling
payRules.testedWith: Tested with sample values: grossSalary 5000, baseSalary 5000, workDays 22, standardMonthlyHours 160, overtimeMultiplier 1.5, and 10 for any other number it uses (#OT_QTY, #YTD_…).
payRules.syntaxHelp: Reference values and call functions with # — e.g. #grossSalary or #pct(#grossSalary, 6.2). Standard operators + - * / %, comparisons and ? : work too.
payRules.insertHint: Click any item to insert it at the cursor.
payRules.dynamicHint: Pay-component codes are also available as variables — e.g. #BASIC, #OT, #TAX_PIT, and #YTD_ year-to-date totals. A payroll input adds #CODE_QTY and #CODE_RATE: hours recorded without a rate (e.g. #OT_QTY) are paid by the component's formula, while an input with an amount, or hours and a rate, is paid as recorded instead of the formula.

byTemplate.TAX_PIT: For employees in {{ country }}, income tax is computed by the {{ country }} payroll template; tax brackets and rules here don't apply to them.
byTemplate.EMPLOYER_CHARGE: For employees in {{ country }}, employer contributions are computed by the {{ country }} payroll template; rules here don't apply to them.

engine.BASIC: Calculated by the payroll engine from each employee's compensation — no formula needed.
engine.BONUS: Paid from bonus awards recorded for the period — no formula needed.
engine.OT: Paid from approved overtime records — add a rule only for a custom overtime formula.
engine.TAX_PIT: Calculated from the income-tax brackets of the employee's country — no formula needed.
engine.ALLOWANCE: Paid from payroll inputs recorded for the period — add a rule for a computed allowance.
engine.DEDUCTION: Taken from deduction records — add a rule for a computed deduction.
engine.EMPLOYER_CHARGE: No employer charge is computed yet — add a rule to calculate one.

templates.title: Payroll template in use: {{ countries }}
templates.taxes: For employees in {{ countries }}, the template computes income tax and employer contributions from the law. Rules here on income tax and employer contributions don't apply to them.
templates.earnings: Their earnings are worked out first, formula rules included. The template taxes the earnings switched to Taxable and charges contributions on those switched to Subject to social contributions.
templates.deductions: Formula deductions come off net pay after the template. They don't lower the tax or contributions it computes.
templates.others: Employees in other countries than {{ countries }} are calculated with the rules and tax brackets here only.

withTemplate.title: How this rule works with the {{ countries }} payroll template

replaced.TAX_PIT: For employees in {{ countries }}, the template computes income tax, so this rule doesn't apply to them. For employees in other countries, it applies where no tax brackets or withholdings calculate their income tax.
replaced.EMPLOYER_CHARGE: For employees in {{ countries }}, the template computes employer contributions, so this rule doesn't apply to them. It applies to employees in other countries.

withTemplate.earning: For employees in {{ countries }}, the rule runs before the template and its amount is added to their gross pay.
withTemplate.taxed: This component is Taxable: the template includes it in the pay it taxes.
withTemplate.untaxed: This component isn't Taxable: the template leaves it out of the pay it taxes. Switch on Taxable in the rules overview if it should be taxed.
withTemplate.social: It's Subject to social contributions: the template charges contributions on it.
withTemplate.nonSocial: It isn't Subject to social contributions: the template charges no contributions on it.
withTemplate.byCode: Some templates treat bonus and overtime pay apart from regular pay, as their country's law does (for example, a bonus as a one-off payment). The template's page says how.
withTemplate.deduction: For employees in {{ countries }}, the rule runs after the template and comes off net pay. It doesn't lower the income tax or contributions the template computes.
withTemplate.variables: A formula can't use the template's results: #taxableIncome is gross pay less pre-tax deductions and pay that isn't taxable, worked out before the template runs.
